proof-waiting.chase: One proof run on a PROOF: card in Hand-work whose event hold has stood chase_after_hours (DRE-7967); a record In Review waiting on an event is re-checked by the proof dispatcher's own 12-hour re-check instead (DRE-7951), so the one hold is never run twice.
proof-waiting.clock: The clock starts at the earliest of the card's open 🔬 proof-waiting holds that qualify — every one but a hold naming the CEO's press and a time-only hold whose time is still ahead — and, for a time-only hold whose time has passed, at the later of its post and its time.
proof-waiting.why: A proof that waits on an observation stood still for 2,126.8 hours in one week (DRE-7960) because nothing said when it was overdue; three days is long enough for the event a proof waits on to happen, and a day is when one run is worth trying first.

hand-work-overdue.chase: The sweep's own once-only hand-work-overdue alarm on the card, raised for the operator at config/hand-work-age.json's hours.
hand-work-overdue.clock: The clock starts when the card entered Hand-work, as the sweep's Hand-work alarm reads it; a PROOF: card with a qualifying proof-waiting hold is judged on that hold's clock instead, so it is never listed twice.
hand-work-overdue.why: A person's card stood still in Hand-work for 338.7 hours in one week (DRE-7960); the alarm at a day was the chase and nothing came after it, so three days is when the wait is late and the console says so.

unlanded-work-watchdog.chase: None of its own: the chase is the sweep's existing work-never-landed notice, on that notice's own clock.
unlanded-work-watchdog.clock: The clock starts at the newest commit on the branch that no pull request has ever been opened for, the same time the work-never-landed notice measures its idle minutes from, and for a person's card with no branch at all at the createdAt of its work-never-landed no-branch notice (DRE-7966).
unlanded-work-watchdog.why: Work with no pull request passes no gate and closes no card, and it stood still for 1,060.6 hours in one week (DRE-7960); a day is long enough to open the pull request for work somebody meant to land.
